Maharashtra Boosts Student Support: Up to ₹80,000 for OBC, VJ, NT & SBC Learners Without Government Hostel Seats

03 Nov 2026, 10:29 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Public Services Desk · Source: www.govtschemes.in

4 min read

Key takeaways--- The information above is compiled from the Maharashtra government’s scheme notification and the HMAS portal guidelines. Prospective applicants should always refer to the latest official circulars before submitting an application.

What the scheme is

The Gyan Jyoti Savitribai Phule Aadhaar Yojana is a Maharashtra government programme that provides direct cash assistance to eligible higher‑education students who qualify for a government hostel but do not receive one. The money is transferred to the student’s Aadhaar‑linked bank account and is meant to cover food, rent and other living costs.

Key benefits (confirmed by the state notification)

  • Assistance amount: ₹50,000 – ₹80,000 for a 10‑month academic year, depending on the location of the college.
  • Highest amount (₹80,000) applies to institutions in Mumbai City, Mumbai Suburban, Navi Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Pimpri‑Chinchwad and Nagpur.
  • Additional material allowance:
  • Technical / engineering courses – up to ₹8,000 per year for study material.
  • All other courses – up to ₹4,000 per year.
  • Maximum duration: 5 years for most courses; 6 years for engineering and medical programmes.
  • Seats: 600 per district, totalling 21,600 beneficiaries across 36 districts.

Who can apply (verified eligibility criteria)

Source-listed details
ConditionRequirement
ResidenceMust be a Maharashtra resident.
CategoryOBC, VJ, NT or SBC with a valid caste certificate.
EducationCompleted Class 12 with ≥ 60 % (or equivalent CGPA) and enrolled in a recognised higher‑education course.
IncomeParental annual income ≤ ₹2.50 lakh (subject to any central revision).
AadhaarLinked to a nationalised‑bank account.
Hostel statusEligible for a government hostel but not allotted a seat.
Location ruleStudent must not be a resident of the same city/taluka where the college is located.
Age≤ 30 years at the time of admission.
Other schemesCannot be receiving benefits under the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Swayam Yojana.

How the benefit is paid (process details)

  1. Application – Submit an online form on the HMAS portal (hostel‑management system). The portal requires Aadhaar authentication, personal and academic details, and uploads of supporting documents (caste certificate, income proof, rent affidavit, college admission letter, etc.).
  2. Verification – The Other Backward Bahujan Welfare Department checks eligibility and confirms the hostel‑non‑allocation status.
  3. Disbursement – Approved assistance is released in four instalments over the 10‑month period, with later instalments linked to a minimum 75 % attendance record.
  4. Continuation – Students must maintain ≥ 75 % attendance and pass each academic year. One ATKT is allowed; a second ATKT disqualifies the student from further payments.

Practical implications for students

  • Cash flow: Direct deposit eliminates the need for intermediaries and reduces delays in receiving funds.
  • Housing flexibility: The scheme is designed for students who rent private accommodation, helping them meet rent and food expenses.
  • Academic focus: The attendance and result conditions encourage consistent study habits.
  • Limited overlap: Students already benefitting from the Swayam Yojana must choose one scheme, preventing duplicate subsidies.

How to verify the announcement

  • Visit the official Maharashtra Other Backward Bahujan Welfare Department website and locate the latest circular dated 27 October 2026 (the resolution that raised assistance levels).
  • Check the HMAS portal (https://hmas.maharashtra.gov.in) for the “Gyan Jyoti Savitribai Phule Aadhaar Yojana” banner and the current application schedule.
  • Call the toll‑free helpline 020‑26127569 or email [email protected] for clarification on eligibility or document requirements.

Frequently asked points (reported by the department)

  • Can a student join mid‑year? Yes, provided all eligibility conditions are met.
  • What if there is an education gap? Applicants with a gap can apply if they satisfy the age and other criteria.
  • Is the scheme limited to professional courses? No – both professional and non‑professional courses recognised by the appropriate authority are covered, with 70 % of seats reserved for professional streams.
  • When do the revised rates start? From the academic year 2026‑27.

--- *The information above is compiled from the Maharashtra government’s scheme notification and the HMAS portal guidelines. Prospective applicants should always refer to the latest official circulars before submitting an application.*
